clue.text: Disheartened after skinhead made a hit

indicators.note: after says the cored piece follows the skin's head letter

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word skin
with the heart taken out, as an apple is cored

explanation.surface: A bald-headed thug, feeling low, still landed a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a thug but gives the head of 'skin'; 'after' puts CORED behind that S.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to make a hit, whether a goal, a point or a success.

clue.text: Old king accompanied by personal assistant, an older man

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, a monarch of the past
accompanied by gives the joining word and

explanation.surface: A former monarch travels with his secretary, a gentleman of advanced years.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is an older man of the family, a generation above the parents.

clue.text: Opened up an alfresco feast

parts.note: something done alfresco is done out of doors, out
a spread is a lavish meal laid out on the table

explanation.surface: A picnic banquet was unpacked in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outspread is extended or unfolded, as wings or arms opened wide.

clue.text: Cancel points of entry

parts.note: N and E are compass points, north and east
a gate is a way of entry

explanation.surface: An order to close the places where people come in.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to nullify or cancel it out.

clue.text: There's some point to a flower festival

definitions.text: There's some point to a flower festival

parts.words: There's some point to a flower festival
parts.note: a compass point, east, lies within the name of a spring feast famous for its lilies and flower displays

explanation.surface: Someone defends the worth of a village flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'point' is the compass point EAST, which begins the festival's name; spring flowers, especially lilies, decorate churches for it.
explanation.definitionFit: This Christian spring festival is celebrated with lilies and floral decorations in churches.

clue.text: Get no ale perhaps, and yet get bigger!

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters of 'Get no ale' as one possible arrangement among others

explanation.surface: A drinker is refused beer, yet somehow still grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'Get no ale' to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen, to make or grow longer.

clue.text: Oriental copper-or could be a Spaniard

parts.note: a sen is a small coin of Japan and other Far Eastern countries, a copper's worth
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Eastern coin, or perhaps a gentleman from Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'copper' is a low-value coin; the sen is a hundredth of a yen.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish title for a man, so it stands for a Spaniard.

clue.text: Once 25 called for a stretcher

parts.note: ex- means former, once
the clue at 25 describes a nurse, one who tends the sick, so a tender

explanation.surface: A former nurse was summoned to fetch a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' sends you to the clue at 25-down, a hospital nurse: someone who tends patients is a TENDER. 'stretcher' is not a hospital litter but something that extends.
explanation.definitionFit: An extender lengthens things, just as a stretcher pulls them longer.

clue.text: Though a drinker, the driver should imbibe nothing

indicators.note: imbibe means take in, so the driver's letters swallow the nought

parts.note: a driver is one who uses a car, a car user
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Advice that a motorist who likes a drink should stick to none.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is not the person at the wheel in general but anyone who uses a car; 'should imbibe' signals the nought being swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser is a reveller who drinks heavily and noisily.

clue.text: Like firm agent getting into a mess

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the word agent gets into a muddle, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Just as a company spy ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning similar; 'getting into a mess' is the anagram signal for 'agent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related or akin, of a similar nature or origin.

clue.text: Splits the Right on objectives

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
ends are aims or objectives

explanation.surface: Political factions on the Right quarrel over their aims.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart, so rends means tears or splits.

clue.text: Unfamiliar Argentine fruit

indicators.note: unfamiliar suggests the word Argentine made strange, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: An exotic fruit from South America nobody recognises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfamiliar' rearranges the nine letters of 'Argentine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: Girl in a daring dress

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the words a daring

explanation.surface: A young woman wearing a bold outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a woman's given name, crossword shorthand for a girl.

clue.text: Left some absorbed in a legal document

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken into the middle of the document's letters

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
part means some of something

explanation.surface: Someone walked out partway through reading a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as a direction but means went away; 'absorbed in' signals one piece taken into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means went away, the same as left.

clue.text: A revolutionary artist?

parts.note: read as a painter of radical views, but really an English landscape painter whose surname also means one who rotates things

explanation.definitionFit: J. M. W. Turner was a great English painter, and a craftsman on a lathe makes things revolve.

clue.text: Of one mind about sum a union should raise

indicators.note: about signals the letters of sum, a and union moved around

explanation.surface: A trade union agrees together on how much money to raise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SUM, A and UNION; 'should raise' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimous means fully in agreement, with everyone sharing a single view.

clue.text: Lawyers, over a period, created peers

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers, lawyers
on can mean over, resting on top of
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Barristers, after some years, were elevated to the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The baronage is the whole body of barons, the nobility or peers of the realm.

clue.text: This member's to be seen in the bar most evenings

indicators.note: to be seen in says the limb can be spotted within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A club member who props up the bar on most nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be seen in' points to the letters inside 'bar most'; 'evenings' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is a limb, a member of the body.

clue.text: The occupant let the players in

indicators.note: in says the team goes inside the word for letting

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: A tenant allowed the actors into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' reads as allowed but means rented out; 'in' signals the team going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is one who lives in a place, its occupant.

clue.text: A retired man's hideaway

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ned is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A pensioner's private retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns NED round.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a private room or lair where one can withdraw from others.

clue.text: Quietly read letters about a show

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: about says the letters of read and a are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone reads softly about a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges READ and A into ARADE, after P; 'letters' just says it is the word's letters being used.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a public procession or display, a show.

clue.text: Ring in about some eggs

indicators.note: in says the ring is placed inside the word for about

parts.note: re means about or concerning
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone telephones about a few eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside RE; 'Ring' is a shape, not a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs in a fish's ovary.

clue.text: Very friendly. It's the drink!

explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly, and is also a sweet fruit concentrate diluted to drink.

clue.text: Thoughts of a Greek character into vegetables

indicators.note: into says the Greek letter goes inside the vegetables

parts.note: onions are bulb vegetables
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek actor muses over a pile of greengrocery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vegetables' is a plural, so the Greek letter must land inside a plural word; 'into' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions are views or beliefs, the thoughts one holds on a matter.

clue.text: A top man, political leader, given nicer accommodation

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of political
accommodation suggests the letters of nicer being rehoused in a new order

explanation.surface: A senior figure and party head is given better lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes P from 'political'; 'accommodation' rearranges NICER into RINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a royal ruler or leading figure, one at the very top.

clue.text: She's helpful with complaints, relatively speaking

explanation.definitionFit: A ward sister is a senior nurse who treats illnesses, and a sister is a female family relation.

clue.text: Such a vessel may be ancient or newly-built

indicators.note: newly-built says the letters of ancient or are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A ship that might be very old or freshly constructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-built' rearranges the letters of 'ancient or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A container is any receptacle that holds something, as a vessel does.

clue.text: An article about a note's number

indicators.note: about says the article goes around the note

parts.note: the is the definite article
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a musical note's value.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the sol-fa note; 'about' signals the article going round it, and the 's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a number, the integer after two.

clue.text: He knew how to lay his hands on a fortune!

definitions.text: He knew how to lay his hands on a fortune!

parts.words: He knew how to lay his hands on a fortune!
parts.note: sounds like a shrewd financier, but describes the king of myth whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend King Midas was granted a golden touch, so all he handled became gold.

clue.text: Polonius's son determined actual returns

indicators.note: returns says the whole phrase determined actual comes back reversed

parts.note: set means fixed or determined
real means actual

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's verdict on a character's real comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the whole of 'determined actual' backwards as one string; Polonius and his son appear in Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Hamlet, Laertes is the son of the courtier Polonius and brother of Ophelia.

clue.text: Exact account given by a minister

parts.note: a curate is a clergyman, a minister assisting a parish priest

explanation.surface: A precise statement provided by a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means precise and correct, the same as exact.

clue.text: Quite proper depression about the church

indicators.note: about says the hollow goes around the church

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Feeling low about church is entirely respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England; 'about' signals the hollow going round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means respectable and fitting, quite proper in behaviour.
